title: tangos.json
description: tangOS repo descriptor. One file per decomp repo that normalizes it into a single vocabulary read by every tangOS app (Console, Docs, Atlas). A repo's own tools are declared in `tools[]`; tangOS turns each entry into an MCP tool generically.

project.description: Human-facing identity + matching guidance. Superset of Chaos Viewer's project.config.json.

githubClientId.description: Optional GitHub OAuth app client_id for Console's "Sign into GitHub" device flow.

workUnit.description: What one piece of work is in this project: a single function (the classic match-one-function flow), a class, or a whole translation unit (a source file that holds several functions). Absent means "function". Console reads it to decide whether to hand out functions or units; a project that is fully matched and now converts code to real classes says "class" or "tu".

languageMode.description: The language new source is written in: "c" (plain C, the function-match default), "cpp" (class-first C++: real methods, compiler-spelled names) or "mixed" (both occur; Console falls back to reading `language`). More exact than the free-text `language`, which stays the display string.

compilerPin.description: The canonical compiler build, as the folder name under tools/<requirements.compiler>/, e.g. "2004/b56". Console's preflight checks that exact build is installed. Absent means the `version` default of the `match` tool is used, as before.

srcPathTool.description: Tool id that says where a source file for a symbol belongs (a repo whose src/ is bucketed by domain or by translation unit cannot be told in one sentence of `matchConventions.srcLayout`). Takes the symbol as its first positional argument.

gates.description: Checks that must pass before work is published, in order. Each names a tool from this descriptor. `when` says at which point it runs: pre-push (before a branch is pushed), pre-pr (before a pull request is opened) or pre-merge (what the maintainers run before landing). Console lists them in the brief and offers them as ready-made calls; it does not run a merge gate for you.

tool.description: A tool id from this descriptor's tools[].

description.description: What a failure means and how to read it.

pr.description: Pull request shape for projects whose PRs are not "matched N functions". Surfaced to the AI next to `submitting`; Console does not open the PR itself when matchConventions.autoPr is false.

titleTemplate.description: Title pattern with placeholders such as {classes}, {functions}, {tus}.

bodyTemplate.description: Body outline: what to say and what proof to attach (gate results, ROM evidence).

setup.description: How a contributor gets the repo runnable.

verifyCommand.description: Template command that verifies one function matches (placeholders like {name} {addrHex} {sizeHex}).

rules.description: Legal / contribution rules (ROM ownership, what may be committed).

submitting.description: How to open a PR: format, what may land in src/, where near-misses go. Surfaced to connected AIs at MCP startup and in next_batch. Point at an AGENTS.md in the repo for the full guide.

knownWalls.description: Proven-unreachable codegen shapes; surfaced to connected AIs via next_batch.

matchConventions.description: Optional matching conventions (attempt-tree logging, near-miss tip store, Ghidra scaffolds). Classic repos omit this; experimental forks set attemptTree so Console/next_batch surface MATCH_RESULT rules once per batch. Unknown extra keys are allowed: repos may keep private conventions here for their own tools; Console ignores what it does not read.

attemptTree.description: When true, MCP startup + next_batch include attempt-tree / MATCH_RESULT logging rules (shared once, not per target).

attemptsPath.description: Append-only attempt log path. Default: config/match_attempts.jsonl.

provenancePath.description: Final how-record path on bank. Default: config/match_provenance.jsonl.

ghidraDrafts.description: When true, agents may use local ghidra_out/ scaffolds as structure hints only (never bank as-is).

nearMissDb.description: Near-miss tip store path. Default: nearmiss/db.jsonl.

srcLayout.description: Where a matched source file belongs, e.g. "src/arm9/<symbol>.c|.cpp and src/arm7/<symbol>.c|.cpp, one matched function each". Emitted to the agent as its own WHERE A MATCH GOES directive in every batch: a repo that splits src/ by CPU or segment does not build a file dropped at the top of src/, and the byte gate does not catch the misplacement (it resolves each file from its own decomp marker, not from where the file sits).

autoPr.description: Whether Console may open pull requests for this project. Absent or true keeps the function-match flow (Writes + Review + Push on: a rolling per-agent PR of verified one-function files). false locks the Push toggle: the project publishes class and translation-unit work through its own integrator, and Console makes no PR of its own. Local verification and banking are unaffected.

defaultProvenance.description: Prefill matchProvenance slugs for attempt-tree nodes (model / reasoning / harness).

runtime.description: How tangOS executes this repo's tools.

cwd.description: Working directory for tool commands, relative to the repo root. Default ".".

python.description: Python interpreter to use, e.g. "python", "python3", or a venv path. Default "python".

shell.description: Run commands through a shell (enables pipes/redirection). Default false (argv spawn).

envKeys.description: Names of environment variables some tools need (e.g. API keys). Values are NEVER stored here; tangOS reads them from the user's environment or prompts.

envKeyHelp.description: Per-key guidance for entries in envKeys, keyed by env var name: what the key unlocks and where to obtain it. Shown in Console's key vault UI. Values are still NEVER stored in the descriptor.

note.description: What the key is for / when it is needed.

requirements.description: What the repo needs locally to actually run its tools. Surfaced to the user as a preflight checklist. tangOS does NOT ship any of these.

rom.description: Requires a user-supplied extracted ROM / game dump.

compiler.description: Name of a required external compiler the user must install, e.g. "mwccarm".

data.description: How tangOS Atlas obtains normalized progress/function data for this repo.

generate.description: Command that (re)generates the normalized data file. May use {out}.

dbPath.description: Repo-relative path the generate command writes to.

committedDbUrl.description: URL of a committed/published data file (e.g. a raw GitHub URL on a data branch). Lets tangOS pull the whole team's live progress/contributions. Highly recommended for collaborative projects.

claimsApi.description: Base URL of a claims/coordination service (e.g. https://belongto.us/api/claims) with a read-only GET /check?module=&start=&end= endpoint. Lets tangOS show who is working where.

projectId.description: This project's id on the claims service (e.g. "pictochat"). The service hosts one board per decomp; this scopes claim reads to this project's board. Absent means the service's primary project, which is what pre-project descriptors have always got.

liveApi.description: This project's live stream on the tangos backend, e.g. https://tangos.dev/api/projects/pictochat. Publish events only: it says when this project's own CI has landed a fresh chaos-db, so the Atlas reloads then instead of waiting out its poll. Separate from claimsApi on purpose - that one brings claims, cosmetics and counts, which belong only to the project the backend serves.

claimsMdUrl.description: Raw URL of the live CLAIMS.md. Optional: if absent the console derives it from committedDbUrl (same owner/repo, main branch, /CLAIMS.md).

tiers.description: Which per-function tier columns this project's chaos-db publishes beyond `matched`. The Atlas offers a colour mode for each one declared; when absent it looks for the columns in the data itself. A column is a boolean on each function record that is present only when true (absent means no).

converted.description: Records carry `converted`: the source is readable (a real name, no raw offsets, no unk_ fields, no codegen tricks).

linked.description: Records carry `linked`: the function's translation unit reaches the port or recompilation binary.

units.description: Records carry `class`, `tuId` and `tuState`, so the Atlas can outline and group by translation unit.

categories.description: Optional display metadata for tool categories (order + label). Categories referenced by tools but absent here still render with defaults.

console.description: Which of this repo's tools fill the jobs tangOS Console drives. Every value is a tool id from this descriptor's own tools[]. All optional: a repo that fills none still gets the Viewer, the tool catalog and MCP, it just doesn't offer the parts it has no tool for. Console falls back to the historical sm64ds ids (coddog / refine_wl / worklist / match / log_attempt) for any role left unset, so descriptors written before this block keep working.

scheduler.description: Ranks unmatched functions and writes a worklist. Without this (or any read-only tool taking `out` and `limit`) Console cannot generate batches.

refineScheduler.description: Scheduler for the Refiner role: near-misses that already carry a draft.

randomScheduler.description: Scheduler for the Random role: any unmatched function, no similarity bias. Usually streams JSONL to stdout rather than taking an `out` arg.

enrich.description: Expands one target into a full worklist row, given `module` and `addr` values. Used for functions hand-picked in the Viewer, which the scheduler never produced.

driver.description: Runs an agent over a worklist via an API key. Receives `wl`, `out`, `jobs` and `attempts` values.

land.description: Banks a finished drive: matched sources into src/, near-misses into the draft store. Receives `out` and `wl` values.

verify.description: Verifies one candidate against the ROM. The merge gate.

unitScheduler.description: Ranks classes or translation units (project.workUnit "class" / "tu") and writes a unit worklist, the way `scheduler` ranks functions.

unitVerify.description: Verifies a whole unit against the ROM and prints one machine-readable verdict (see the tool's `successPattern`).

unitPromote.description: Enrolls a verified unit into the build. Mutating: should declare `previewFlag` or `apply`.

unitReview.description: Source review of a unit by someone who did not write it (readability and fidelity, separate from the byte check).

tools.description: The repo's tool registry. Each entry becomes one MCP tool in Console and one card in Docs.

id.description: Unique, MCP-tool-safe id (snake_case). Becomes the exposed tool name.

description.description: What the tool does - shown to the AI and in Docs.

readOnly.description: True if the tool only reads/reports and never mutates repo state (writes src/, commits, appends ledgers, hits mutating APIs). Drives the safety UI.

command.description: Command template. Supported placeholders: {python} (runtime.python), {flags} (rendered args), and {argName} for any declared arg. Example: "{python} tools/progress.py {flags}".

apply.description: For mutating tools that support a dry run: the flag that turns the dry run into a real mutation (e.g. "--apply"). tangOS defaults these tools to dry-run and requires explicit confirmation to pass this flag.

previewFlag.description: For a tool that MUTATES by default and offers a flag that only previews (e.g. "--dry-run"). The opposite of `apply`: tangOS passes this flag unless the caller explicitly confirms a real run, so a tool that applies unless told otherwise still defaults to a preview.

successPattern.description: Regular expression (JavaScript syntax) that matches the tool's output when it succeeded, for tools whose exit code does not say (e.g. "UNIT VERDICT: bytes=ok"). Console scores a run as a pass when it matches.

longRunning.description: Hint that this tool streams for a long time (orchestrators, batch runs). Default false.

needs.description: Preflight capabilities this tool requires: "rom", "compiler", "network", or "env:VAR_NAME".

args.description: Declared arguments. Rendered into {flags} in declaration order; also individually addressable as {argName}.

name.description: Arg name (snake_case). Also the MCP parameter name.

type.description: Value type. "boolean" renders the flag with no value when true; "enum" constrains to `choices`.

flag.description: CLI flag this arg renders as, e.g. "--module". Omit for a positional argument.

positional.description: Render as a bare positional value (no flag). Default false.

default.description: Default value when the arg is omitted.
